newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore refiners to cut output if losses persist.
newsitem.headline: Singapore refiners to cut output if losses persist.

text.p: Singapore oil refiners, facing operating losses for the first time in four months, might cut production within a month if business does not pick up, industry sources said on Tuesday.
"We are looking at it (losses) closely. If we think this is the general direction of the market then we will cut runs quickly," one refining source said.
"But we have to make sure we have the products and can cut the crude supply or sell the crude," he said.

Industry sources said Singapore refiners on Monday were incurring losses of up to 60 cents per barrel of crude refined, at the basic stage of refining, compared to profits of more than $2.00 in April.

The margins squeeze has developed because crude prices have been rising and oil products prices have not. Singapore's Ministry of Trade and Industry said that profit margins were expected to be low for the next six months.

"Local refineries expect to see a decline in fuel margins with regional refineries returning from maintenance shutdowns by the third quarter of 1997," it said in a statement that accompanied its quarterly outlook of the economy.
